# What is actually established

**Date:** 11 August 2026 · **Corpus / protocol counts:** see `results/canonical.txt` (regenerated by `make experiments`)
**Gate:** 158 tests; gate non-vacuity, schema, coherence, visibility, twins, coverage, conservation, declarations, pruning, docsync, staleness

A single honest ledger of claim strength, so that nothing in this project gets
quoted at a confidence it has not earned. Three tiers, and the middle one is the
largest.

---

## Tier 1 — Conclusive

These follow from structure and are checked mechanically. Overturning one means
finding a bug, not gathering more data.

### C1. The conservation boundary

> Where two worlds project to identical evidence **and differ in whether any
> account diverges from the record**, no evidence-determined mechanism resolves
> both. Where they differ only in the *intent* behind a divergence both exhibit,
> a non-attributive vocabulary resolves both at no cost.

Proof is one line: identical evidence yields one verdict, so the question is
whether one verdict can be correct in both worlds, and the divergence signature
D decides it. Checked across 10 twin pairs × 18 protocols;
`docs/findings/12-conservation-boundary.md`.

**Why this is the project's central result.** It converts T8 from a conjecture
supported by examples into a boundary that predicts where mechanisms can and
cannot win — and the prediction is checkable, which a tautology would not be.

### C2. No evidence-determined mechanism separates a verified twin pair

A corollary, but worth stating separately because it is what makes the harness
trustworthy. If any protocol ever solved both sides of a verified binding pair,
it would be reading outside the `EvidenceView`. This is now a standing check
rather than a hope.

### C3. B13's residual is characterised, not enumerated

Witness-carrying messages fail exactly the classes where some party asserts
nothing about the artifact in dispute. Recomputation needs an assertion to
check. This is a property of the mechanism, not a list of six class labels, and
it held when four new classes were added on the other party's side.

### C4. The scorer is total and its semantics are pinned

Every reachable (truth, verdict) state has exactly one label, verified by
enumeration and fixed by a SHA-256 snapshot.

### C5. The correctness gate is tested for failure propagation

The publication review found that a failing declaration audit could be masked by `| tail` even
though the validator itself returned non-zero. The Makefile now uses `pipefail`, and `gate-selftest`
deliberately executes a failing left-hand pipeline and requires the build to observe the failure.
This does not prove every future build composition is correct; it pins the exact masking failure that
occurred.

---

## Tier 2 — Well-supported, corpus-dependent

Robust within what has been modelled. A different corpus could move the numbers,
though the direction is unlikely to reverse.

### S1. The regression (F01)

B0 (bearer token + provider log) 0/100 on the four **assertional** principal-side classes; B1
(PeerReview-style) 100/100. On the four non-assertional principal-side classes, both B0 and B1
score 0/100; B13 reaches 50/100 and B17 reaches 100/100. Unchanged across five corpus versions and the entire
hardening refactor. **The most durable empirical claim in the project**, and the
one that motivated it.

*Limit:* it demonstrates a property of a modelled default, not a measurement of
any deployed system.

### S2. The non-attributive vocabulary is strictly better

Over-attribution falls to zero at no cost in resolution. B17 wrongs five honest
classes and still records a 0% false-attribution rate, because it never names
anyone; an attributive version would have produced 125 false accusations.

*Limit:* "better" assumes false accusation is worse than a weaker claim. That is
a value judgement the harness cannot make.

### S3. Selective disclosure crosses over around scope 8

Query-based and witness-carrying protocols cost more than full disclosure on
small records and less on large ones, crossing near 8 operations.

*Limit:* the byte model is stipulated, not a wire format. The crossover point
moves with the encoder; the existence of a crossover does not.

### S4. Cardinality binding and its price

A sound sorted-leaf commitment publishes |set|. Padding hides it at 2.5–7.6×
proof size. The query-based family loses two classes each when padded; B13 and
the full-disclosure family lose none.

*Limit:* one padding strategy at one width.

### S5. Duty to answer relocates rather than resolves

Five guilty classes resolved, five honest twins broken, exactly one-for-one, on
both sides of the relationship. **This is now a consequence of C1, not
independent evidence** — all five pairs are binding pairs, so no other outcome
was available.

---

## Tier 3 — Not established

Stated because the temptation to quote these is real.

### N1. Any prevalence claim

How often principals genuinely misremember is unmeasured, and it is the
parameter every deployment-safety argument turns on. Without it, "mechanism X
would prevent Y wrongful accusations in practice" is unsupported. **This is the
single largest gap** and no amount of harness work closes it.

### N2. Absolute disclosure cost

Bytes are comparable between protocols under one encoder. They are not a cost
model for anything real.

### N3. Complete channel and fair-exchange behaviour

Four classes now model one-sided abort / receipt-loss on the two legs of the witness chain
(M30–M33), so the original RC-H7 abort caveat is closed. They establish that B13 misses the
executor-abort leg (M30) and that acknowledgement abort/loss forms a binding pair (M32/M33).

What is **not** established is a general channel model: there are still no delay, replay,
retransmission, deadline, reordering, or adversarial-scheduling classes, and no faithful
fair-exchange baseline. Finding 13 is therefore evidence about the specific abort/loss shapes
modelled, not about channel fairness in general.

### N4. Level invariance (T12)

No mechanism in the set introduces a new trusted party except B16c, whose
entitlement is declared rather than analysed. Fair exchange is the test and it
is unwritten.

### N5. That classes span the adversarial space

The coverage audit derives the space and finds 8 of 106 structurally possible
cells occupied. Most gaps are uninteresting; one was not, and it was only found
by looking (RC-H9). Others may remain.

### N6. The gate's own correctness

The gate now runs a non-vacuity self-test plus eleven validation/test stages, which makes the gate
itself load-bearing for every claim above. Two defects have been found in it: **RC-H15**, a masked exit status that let a
correct validator fail silently, and **RC-H16**, a numeric check that did not parse the figure it
was meant to guard. Both presented as a green run.

`gate-selftest` pins the first failure mode and the derived test count pins the second. Neither
generalises to the next integration mistake, and by construction a defect of this class is
invisible while it is active.

### N7. Anything external

Every audit here is self-audit, including the audits of the audits. No
independent implementation, no external review, no third-party test vectors for
the Merkle code. The A2A extension package is an in-repository reference transport and parity
adapter, not an independent implementation or deployment. Its internal uses and proposed next
connections are catalogued in [`extension-use-map.md`](extension-use-map.md).

## Three errors, one shape

| | claimed | actually |
|---|---|---|
| F-H3 | M1/M16 is an evidential twin | M1 conceals, M16 admits; never a twin |
| RC-H9 | withholding is modelled | executor-only, 0/650 for the principal |
| RC-H10 | M22 resists every mechanism | resists the commitment-only family; solved by full disclosure at the cost of M23 |

Every one is a universal claim inferred from the subset in view, and every one
was found by **deriving the structure and diffing it against the declaration** —
never by re-reading the prose, and never by the tests that existed at the time.

The remedy applied each time was to make the claim recomputable. `make check`
now recomputes the corpus size, the class count, the twin declarations, the
withholding balance, the conservation boundary, and every headline figure in the
live documents. A stale number now fails a build rather than surviving in a
document.

**RC-H12 is closed.** The four declarations it named — `PRINCIPAL_LIAR`,
`mutation_family`, `ENTITLEMENTS`, and `src/commitments.py`'s vocabulary — are now
derived-and-diffed or pinned by regression tests. Two required correction; see
[finding 13](findings/13-abort-and-declarations.md).

---

## What would change the picture most

1. **A faithful fair-exchange baseline and a richer channel model.** Finding 13
   measured the specific abort/loss gap at M30–M33; the next useful test is whether
   an actual fair-exchange construction closes M30 without merely relocating the
   failure under delay, replay, retransmission, or scheduling faults.
2. **Stateful evaluation across repeated interactions.** B11 is scored per
   scenario, so its pattern detection cannot show its value. Whether repetition
   genuinely escapes C1 or merely shifts the unit of analysis is the most
   interesting open question in the project.
3. **Real traces (N1).** Outside the harness entirely, and the only thing that
   makes any deployment claim sayable.

---

## Publication readiness

The claim tiers above decide this, so the verdict belongs here.

**Publishable now, as an artifact and negative-results contribution.** The harness and corpus are
a real instrument: deterministic, adversarially structured, and aimed at a question that signed
authorization and provenance artifacts do not answer by themselves: what happens when the parties
disagree about the record. The negative results reproduce. The historical comparison - that
self-defence for a correct party appears in four research lines from 1996-2010, while the specific
identity/delegation proposals originally reviewed here did not cite them - remains useful. A broad
absence claim is no longer appropriate: 2026 now includes DRP, HDP, AP2/Verifiable Intent and
active standards work. See `prior-art/2026-protocol-landscape.md`.

**Not publishable as a cryptography result.** No new primitive was found, and the conservation
boundary has a one-line proof once stated. A reviewer will correctly note that "a function of X
cannot distinguish inputs identical in X" is not a deep theorem. The contribution is the framing -
accountability mechanisms as functions of an evidence projection, with the projection's fibres
determining achievable verdicts - and the fact that the boundary is *checkable* as a build stage.
Presenting it as an impossibility result would oversell it.

**Three things are load-bearing before submission anywhere:**

1. **Reconcile the M-class taxonomy** against the authoritative list. Every result is conditional
   on a reconstruction.
2. **One external reader**, ideally trying to break the visibility invariant. Six self-corrections
   is evidence the method works and evidence that a single author misses things for weeks.
3. **Put prevalence (N1) in the abstract**, not only in limitations. It decides whether any of this
   matters in deployment, and burying it commits the overclaim this study exists to criticise.

**Venue shape:** artifact or benchmark track, a systematisation or negative-results venue, or an
agentic-security workshop. arXiv preprint plus the repository is a reasonable first move.
